note: A mailbox nobody has written anything for: 100 invented emails, six senders, no preset and no hand-written parser anywhere near it. Every sender sits on one side of one gate, so a failure names which gate broke rather than 'the pipeline is off'. Nothing here is real mail — no merchant anyone visited, no names, no account numbers. Amounts are near-unique on purpose: real transaction figures almost never repeat (blu shows 50 distinct in 55 emails), and an earlier draft drew from a short price list, which made the happy-path sender fail a gate for a reason no real sender would.

senders.nusabank.example.com: 25 purchases, one layout — the happy path. Plus 2 refunds and 2 incoming, both DELIBERATELY below the volume floor: a sender's rare layouts are invisible to the loop, and this is where that shows.
senders.kirimin.example.com: 20 emails, one subject, TWO layouts (10 rides / 10 food orders). A sender is not one template.
senders.promo.tokobagus.example.com: 15 emails, templated, full of Rp, the same three prices every time. Must be refused on amount variance.
senders.warungkopi.example.com: 6 genuine receipts. Must be refused on VOLUME — waits rather than guesses. Its amounts are fine.
senders.kabar.example.com: 20 newsletters, no currency anywhere. Must be dropped by the currency filter before anything else runs.
senders.dompetku.example.com: 10 top-ups. Amounts move; the counterparty is the same string every time. Any pattern anchored on it reads a label, and the constant-merchant check must refuse it.
